title: Everyday Worship
description: Little Muslim → Beginner. Short questions about daily prayer, wudu, the prayer direction, Ramadan routines, simple duas and words of remembrance. Children learn and practice with adult guidance; prepubescent children are not treated as having adult fasting obligations. Written with children around ages 6–9 in mind; an adult may read questions aloud. All questions are Beginner level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Uses introductory worship knowledge, short wording and straightforward examples for the Kids audience. Age and level are editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith reports checked during preparation. Questions describe ordinary worship practice and introductory meanings, not a full manual of legal details or exceptions. Fasting scenarios concern learning or family routines and do not instruct young children to complete adult fasts. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: How many daily obligatory prayers are there in Islam?
questions.explanation: Islam has five obligatory daily prayers, spread across the day and night. Children learn them with guidance.

questions.question: Which prayer belongs to dawn, before sunrise?
questions.explanation: Fajr is the dawn prayer. Its time ends when the sun begins to rise.

questions.question: Which prayer begins after the sun sets?
questions.explanation: Maghrib is the prayer after sunset.

questions.question: What is the familiar call inviting Muslims to prayer called?
questions.explanation: The adhan is the call to prayer. The Prophet ﷺ instructed Bilal to give this call.

questions.question: What is wudu for?

options.text: Finding a mosque on a map

questions.explanation: Wudu involves washing and wiping particular body parts to prepare for prayer. A teacher or parent can show the steps.

questions.question: What is the prayer direction toward the Kaaba called?
questions.explanation: The qiblah is the direction Muslims face in prayer, toward the Kaaba in Makkah.

questions.question: Which prayer movement includes placing the forehead and nose on the ground?
questions.explanation: Sujud means prostration. The forehead and nose touch the ground, along with the other points taught by the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.question: Which month is known as the month of fasting?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the month of obligatory fasting. Not everyone has the same obligations or circumstances.

questions.question: During a normal fasting day, when do Muslims avoid food and drink?
questions.explanation: Fasting includes avoiding food and drink from dawn until sunset. Dawn is earlier than sunrise.

questions.question: What is the meal before dawn for a person who plans to fast called?
questions.explanation: Suhur is the meal before dawn. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged it and described it as blessed.

questions.question: What do we call breaking the fast at sunset?
questions.explanation: Iftar is breaking the fast at sunset. The Prophet ﷺ taught not to delay it unnecessarily once its time arrives.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when going to bed?

options.text: Asked the stars to protect him
Said bedtime was never for remembrance
Taught that dua was only for mosques

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ remembered Allah with a dua before sleeping. We can learn a bedtime dua with an adult's help.

questions.question: Which pair follows the Prophet's ﷺ teaching when starting to eat?

options.text: Mention Allah's name and use the right hand
Boast loudly and grab from everyone
Skip Allah's name and mock the food
Push others away and take their portions

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught a child to mention Allah's name, eat with the right hand and eat from what was nearest.

questions.question: After eating or drinking, whom do we praise and thank?
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to praise Allah for food and drink. Saying Alhamdulillah expresses that praise.

questions.question: What does dhikr mean in worship?
questions.explanation: Dhikr is remembrance of Allah. The Quran teaches us to remember Him often.

questions.question: Which phrase glorifies Allah and declares Him free from imperfection?
questions.explanation: Subhanallah glorifies Allah as perfect and free from any imperfection. It is a phrase of remembrance.

questions.question: What does Allahu akbar mean?
questions.explanation: Allahu akbar declares Allah's greatness. We say it in worship and remembrance.

questions.question: Which phrase means asking Allah for forgiveness?
questions.explanation: Astaghfirullah means that we seek Allah's forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness after prayer.

questions.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ teach us to go to prayer?
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught calmness when going to prayer, even when the prayer is starting.

questions.question: In the Quran's dua for parents, what do we ask Allah to give them?
questions.explanation: The Quran teaches a dua asking Allah to show our parents mercy, remembering their care when we were small.

questions.question: Are the five daily prayers meant to be one single prayer at one time?

options.text: No, they are prayers across the day and night
Yes, five is only another name for one
Yes, all five belong only at midnight
No, they are five prayers only once a year

questions.explanation: The five obligatory prayers belong across each day and night. Their number is five, rather than one combined daily prayer.

questions.question: Does Fajr's normal time continue after sunrise begins?

options.text: No, it ends when the sun begins to rise
Yes, it starts only after sunrise

questions.explanation: Fajr belongs before sunrise. Its normal time ends as the sun begins to rise.

questions.question: What event marks the start of Maghrib time?

options.text: The sky is bright at lunchtime

questions.explanation: Maghrib begins after sunset. We can learn local prayer times with a parent or teacher.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the adhan?

options.text: To announce that a meal is ready
To name the months of the year
To count how many people own books

questions.explanation: The adhan invites people to salah. It is connected with prayer, rather than a meal announcement.

questions.question: Which action belongs to wudu?
questions.explanation: Washing the face is part of wudu. Other parts are washed or wiped as taught.

questions.question: Does facing the Kaaba mean Muslims worship the building?

options.text: Yes, the building receives our worship
No, Muslims worship Allah and face the qiblah
No, we worship the sun instead

questions.explanation: We worship Allah alone. The Kaaba gives us the direction to face in prayer, rather than an object to worship.

questions.question: In sujud, where does the forehead rest?

options.text: On top of another person's head
In the air above the floor

questions.explanation: In sujud, the forehead and nose rest on the ground. We learn the posture carefully with a teacher.

questions.question: Does learning about Ramadan mean every young child must fast like an adult?

options.text: Yes, age and ability never matter
Yes, a young child's learning has no value without fasting
No, children before puberty do not have adult fasting duties

questions.explanation: Children before puberty are not obliged to fast. They can learn about Ramadan with their family without being treated as adults.

questions.question: Does the daily fast start at dawn or at sunrise?
questions.explanation: The daily fast begins at dawn, earlier than sunrise. Food and drink are avoided until sunset during a normal fast.

questions.question: Which description of suhur is correct?

options.text: The meal that breaks the fast after sunset
A meal before dawn for someone preparing to fast
A name for the afternoon prayer
A way of washing before prayer

questions.explanation: Suhur comes before the fasting day begins. Iftar is different: it breaks the fast at sunset.

questions.question: Should a fasting person wait until midnight to have iftar after sunset has arrived?

options.text: Yes, midnight is always the only time
Yes, the fast never ends at sunset
No, iftar belongs only before dawn

questions.explanation: The daily fast ends at sunset. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged breaking it promptly when its time comes.

questions.question: Can remembering Allah be part of a bedtime routine?

options.text: No, remembrance belongs only in a mosque
No, bedtime can never include dua
Yes, but only if we invent the Prophet's ﷺ words
Yes, we can learn and say a bedtime dua

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ remembered Allah before sleep. We can include a learned dua in our bedtime routine.

questions.question: Why do we mention Allah's name before eating?

options.text: To remember Allah as we begin our meal
To claim that we created the food
To make other people feel unwelcome
To replace learning good table manners

questions.explanation: Mentioning Allah's name brings remembrance into eating. It goes along with the other manners the Prophet ﷺ taught.

questions.question: What does saying Alhamdulillah after food express?

options.text: A claim that we never need help
A request to worship our plate
Permission to mock someone else's food

questions.explanation: We praise Allah for the blessing of food and drink. Alhamdulillah is a way to express that thanks.

questions.question: Which activity is dhikr?

options.text: Inventing sayings and calling them revelation
Counting people only to make fun of them

questions.explanation: Dhikr turns our attention to Allah. It includes remembering Him with words of praise.

questions.question: Does Subhanallah praise Allah as perfect, or describe Him as having faults?

options.text: It describes Him as having faults
It asks the sun for help
It claims that people made the sky

questions.explanation: Subhanallah is glorification of Allah, declaring Him free from faults. It is not a description of any imperfection.

questions.question: Which meaning matches Allahu akbar?

options.text: Asking a friend for a gift

questions.explanation: Allahu akbar is a declaration of Allah's greatness. It is among the words used in worship.

questions.question: Does asking Allah for forgiveness happen only after a huge mistake?

options.text: Yes, it can never be part of daily worship
No, seeking forgiveness is a regular part of worship
Yes, the Prophet ﷺ never did it after prayer
No, it means we should stop trying to do good

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness after prayer. Asking forgiveness can be part of regular worship as we keep trying to do good.

questions.question: If prayer is starting, does that make pushing and rushing a good way to reach it?

options.text: Yes, speed matters more than everyone else's safety
Yes, we must push anyone ahead of us
No, we should still approach calmly
Yes, racing is the purpose of prayer

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught a calm approach even when prayer was starting. We do not need to turn it into a race.

questions.question: What does the Quran's dua for parents help us remember?

options.text: That parents never need kind treatment
That dua is only for ourselves
Their care and our prayer for Allah's mercy for them

questions.explanation: The dua remembers parents' care in childhood and asks Allah to show them mercy.

questions.question: Sara makes a learning chart for the daily obligatory prayers. How many spaces for prayer names does she need?
questions.explanation: There are five daily obligatory prayers. A five-space chart can help Sara learn their names.

questions.question: Ayan sees Fajr listed before sunrise on the prayer timetable. Which description fits?
questions.explanation: Fajr is the dawn prayer, before sunrise. A local timetable helps us learn its time.

questions.question: The sun has just set and your family is preparing to pray. Which prayer is beginning?
questions.explanation: Maghrib begins after sunset. It is different from the dawn and daytime prayers.

questions.question: Maryam hears the adhan with her family. What does this call invite them to do?
questions.explanation: The adhan is the call to prayer. Maryam can learn about salah with her family's help.

questions.question: You need wudu before practicing prayer and are still learning its steps. What is a helpful choice?

options.text: Ask a parent or teacher to show the washing and wiping
Guess that counting fingers is enough
Only wipe your shoes on a rug
Paint your hands instead of washing

questions.explanation: Learn the steps of wudu carefully. A parent or teacher can show which parts to wash and wipe.

questions.question: You are preparing to practice salah in a new place. Which direction should an adult help you find?

options.text: Whichever wall has the brightest paint
Where the most expensive furniture is
The direction of the nearest shop

questions.explanation: Muslims face the qiblah for prayer. An adult can help you find the direction toward the Kaaba.

questions.question: Your teacher asks you to identify prostration in a prayer lesson. Which movement is it?
questions.explanation: Sujud is prostration, with the forehead and nose on the ground. A teacher can help you learn its posture.

questions.question: A family calendar marks the month of fasting. Which month should Lina match with it?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the fasting month. Young children can learn about it with their family without having adult fasting obligations.

questions.question: Your teacher asks when a normal fasting day begins and ends. Which answer fits?
questions.explanation: The fasting day runs from dawn until sunset. Dawn and sunrise are not the same time.

questions.question: Before dawn, your family has a meal to prepare for fasting. What is this meal called?
questions.explanation: The meal before dawn is suhur. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged this meal for those who fast.

questions.question: Your fasting family members are ready to end their fast. Sunset has arrived. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Breaking the fast at sunset is iftar. It does not need to wait until midnight.

questions.question: You want to follow a bedtime habit of the Prophet ﷺ. Which choice fits?

options.text: Ask a lucky charm to guard your bed
Make up words and claim the Prophet ﷺ said them
Say that remembering Allah is never for bedtime
Learn and say a bedtime dua to Allah

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ remembered Allah before sleeping. Ask a parent or teacher to help you learn a bedtime dua.

questions.question: You are about to eat and want to follow the Prophet's ﷺ teaching. What should you do?

options.text: Say Bismillah and eat with your right hand
Boast and grab from another person's plate
Push someone away from the table
Say that remembering Allah has no place at meals

questions.explanation: Mention Allah's name before eating and use your right hand, following the teaching given to a child by the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.question: You finish your meal and want to praise Allah for it. Which phrase fits?

options.text: There is no need to be grateful

questions.explanation: Alhamdulillah praises Allah. Saying it after food is a simple way to express gratitude for His blessing.

questions.question: Your teacher says, "Let us remember Allah." Which kind of worship is being encouraged?
questions.explanation: Remembering Allah is dhikr. We can learn words of remembrance and their meanings.

questions.question: A lesson asks for a phrase glorifying Allah as free from imperfection. Which phrase should you choose?
questions.explanation: Subhanallah is a phrase that glorifies Allah as perfect. Learning its meaning helps us understand our remembrance.

questions.question: You hear Allahu akbar in a worship lesson. Which meaning should you remember?
questions.explanation: Allahu akbar declares Allah's greatness. We learn the words along with their meaning.

questions.question: After prayer, you are learning words for seeking Allah's forgiveness. Which phrase belongs in that lesson?
questions.explanation: Astaghfirullah asks Allah for forgiveness. Seeking forgiveness after prayer follows the Prophet's ﷺ example.

questions.question: You are walking to prayer with an adult and hear that it is starting. What should you do?

options.text: Push people out of your way
Continue calmly without pushing or running
Challenge your friend to race inside

questions.explanation: Approach prayer with calmness. The Prophet ﷺ taught this even when the prayer was beginning.

questions.question: You want to make a dua for your parents using the Quran's lesson. What could you ask Allah?

options.text: Give me a reason to insult others

questions.explanation: Asking Allah to show your parents mercy follows the Quran's dua for them and remembers their care.
